Iris (Product Design): Heads-up from usability: when scanning large batches the relevance chips + export controls create visual clutter. Can we simplify toolbar and add explicit export scope? Figma: https://redwood.ai/s/fig-batch1 :mag:
Ben (Frontend): Agree. Proposed toolbar: left=compact/comfortable toggle, center=selection count, right=Export (scope badge). Keep export column fixed width so expanding rows don't push UI. I'll prototype anchored dropdown.
Rina (Accessibility): A11y notes: export button needs `aria-haspopup` and `aria-expanded`. Announce export actions with an aria-live region: "Export started: 3 vectors". Sparklines ok if they include a `<title>` for screen readers and not rely on color alone.
Cal (Product): From research, default export should be "Selected" if any rows are selected, otherwise fall back to "Visible". Copy tweak: tooltip for relevance -> "Model confidence (higher = more relevant)". Also warn on exports >5000 rows.
Jules (Design Intern): Quick mock: muted chip colors, 24px sparkline in compact rows, small scope badge on export button e.g., `Export • selected: 3`. Uploaded: https://redwood.ai/s/mock-batch-tool.png :art:
Ben (Frontend): CSS snippet I'll try in storybook:
```
.toolbar { position: sticky; top:0; }
.export-dropdown { position: absolute; right: 0; min-width: 220px; }
.row--compact .spark { width:24px; height:24px; }
```
Will also add `aria-controls` on row toggles and move focus into expanded panel.
Rina (Accessibility): Keyboard flow: Enter or ArrowRight to expand, focus first control inside (copy/download). Add skip link `Skip to next row` for power users. We'll run a quick NVDA pass on the prototype.
preview-bot: Storybook preview: https://staging.redwood.ai/builds/1990012345 (includes anchors, sparklines, export scope badge).
Iris (Product Design): Thanks all. Checklist before PR: fixed export column, export aria-labels and aria-live, sparkline `<title>`, default export scope behavior, large-export warning, and gate behind `batch-export-v2`.
